reasons.text: All three parts share the same part type, material, size, unit of measure, make/buy, lifecycle and export classification, so they describe the same stainless sheet metal bracket.
The weights differ by only about 2 percent, which is consistent with the same part modeled slightly differently rather than a different design.
100-008623 and 210-008622 tie on assembly usage, are both Released, and were created on the same date, so the keep rules do not separate them and 100-008623 is a tentative choice.
330-007138 is the oldest but is used in only one assembly, so usage takes priority and it should not be the part kept.

before_merging: Decide with E. Duarte and F. Haddad whether to keep 100-008623 or 210-008622, since usage, lifecycle and creation date are tied.
Confirm the parts are used interchangeably across business units, as 100-008623 belongs to Aerospace Systems while the others belong to Electrical Products.
Have an engineer confirm the small weight differences (1.066 to 1.089 kg) are modeling differences and not a design change such as different holes or bends.
Plan updates to the 7 assemblies that use the parts being retired so they point to the kept part number.
